The World BankImplementation Status & Results ReportLebanon Emergency Assistance Project (P509428)Jun 29, 2026Page 2 of 10 4. KEY ISSUES & STATUS4.1 Implementation Status and Key DecisionsThe Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP) was approved by the World Banks Board of Directors on June 24, 2025, and the Loan Agreement was signed on August 25, 2025. Following parliamentary ratification on December 19, 2025, the project was declared effective on February 26, 2026. Initial implementation is underway, with the first disbursement to the Designated Account processed on May 13, 2026. Given the current operational context, the project is prioritizing procurement and preparatory activities that can be undertaken immediately, positioning investments for accelerated execution once access and security conditions allow. Initial efforts have successfully established the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within the Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), with core staff contracted and additional personnel identified for mobilization as implementation scales up. The project is advancing immediate procurement packages for emergency response services, telecommunications, and the rehabilitation of schools currently used as shelters. Additionally, stage 1 Framework Agreements (FAs) are being launched to pre-identify contractors for civil works and consulting services, enabling rapid deployment as physical access becomes possible. An engineering firm has been mobilized to conduct an ongoing Investment Needs Assessment. This will update damage and recovery needs across key sectors (including water, energy, transport, health, and education) to guide the prioritization of area-based reconstruction activities. Critical technical assistance and planning activities under procurement, including rubble management design and technical assistance and the procurement of high-resolution satellite imagery to assess road access. To ensure robust fiduciary oversight and transparent implementation, procurement is also underway for a Third-Party Monitoring Agent and supplemental WB expanded supervision oversight through a Lenders Engineer.5.
